findings.location: research/interpretations.md section 3 (3.2 'Principal witnesses and their reasoning' and the 3.3 element table), against sections/40-just-judge-merciful-hearer.tex, 'Daniel's prayer and Daniel's people' (PDF p. 27) and that reading's moral sense (PDF p. 30); and proper-components.toml, [[lanes]] key = "just-judge-merciful-hearer"
findings.problem: Standing advisory from study-review iteration 0, half cleared and restated for the remainder. The manifest half is now repaired: the son-and-lord-of-david lane declares Theodoret of Cyrus, Rupert of Deutz and William Durandus, and the just-judge-merciful-hearer lane declares John Chrysostom and Thomas Aquinas, so every name the sections develop is now declared. Chrysostom is also properly recorded for reading 3 in research/interpretations.md 3.2 ('Jerome, In Eph. II on 4:2; Chrysostom, In Eph. hom. 9'). Aquinas is not. research/interpretations.md section 3 still names no Aquinas among that reading's witnesses and its 3.3 element table gives the Offertory row only Jerome, Augustine, Rupert and Durandus, although the study develops Aquinas there at length ('prayer must be made with confidence of obtaining, and that confidence comes from God's mercy', Super Philippenses c. 4, on 4:6) and credits him by name in the reading's moral sense. The evidence itself is sound and I verified it independently in the tracked Dessain 1857 text of the Pauline commentaries: at Phil 4:6 Aquinas writes 'Item debet esse cum fiducia impetrandi, et hoc ex Dei misericordia. [Dan. 9.] Neque enim in justificationibus nostris prosternimus preces ante faciem tuam, sed in miserationibus ...', which is exactly the use the study makes of him and exactly the source role research/scope.md 3.7 records ('Aquinas uses Dan 9:18 as doctrine on prayer; he does not expound Daniel'). Nothing reaches a reader of the PDF as a false claim. What has changed since iteration 0 is the direction of the mismatch: the manifest now declares a witness that the audit record does not carry, so the correspondence the manifest and audit exist to make inspectable is still broken, now at the audit end rather than the manifest end.
findings.required_result: research/interpretations.md section 3 records Thomas Aquinas among the just-judge-merciful-hearer reading's witnesses, with his locus (Super Philippenses c. 4, on 4:6) and the source role research/scope.md 3.7 already gives him -- doctrine on prayer grounded in Dan 9:18, not exegesis of Daniel -- and the 3.3 Offertory row names him accordingly; or, alternatively, Aquinas is removed from that lane's declared authors in proper-components.toml and from the prose and moral sense of sections/40-just-judge-merciful-hearer.tex that develop him.

findings.location: sections/90-apparatus.tex, 'Reception' paragraph ('Bellarmine was read only in O'Sullivan's abridged English of 1866') and the References entry 'St Robert Bellarmine, A Commentary on the Book of Psalms, trans. J. O'Sullivan (1866, abridged)' (PDF pp. 36 and 38)
findings.problem: Bellarmine is the one witness of the study whose delivery is not disclosed, in an apparatus that is otherwise scrupulous about exactly this. The same paragraph names the delivery of every other non-printed reading: Augustine's Latin as 'Migne, PL 36-37 (Wikisource and Corpus Corporum)' and augustinus.it, and then 'Some Latin texts were read in web deliveries of the standard editions (augustinus.it, monumenta.ch, the Corpus Thomisticum) or in optical text layers of printed editions (Rupert, Durandus, Schuster, Gueranger, Irenaeus, Trent)'. Bellarmine's English falls outside both categories of that sentence, so the only statement a reader has is 'read only in O'Sullivan's abridged English of 1866', which reads as the 1866 printing. The leaf's own record says otherwise: research/source-bindings.toml binds the passages to artifact.robert-bellarmine.commentary-on-the-book-of-psalms.2026-09-05-osullivan-ecatholic2000.historical-text-357551e1 and its context states that the text was 'read on reentry (2026-09-18) in the tracked text, re-hashed' and that 'the Latin original was not read'. I verified all ten of the study's Bellarmine quotations in that same tracked transcription, and confirmed that the Ps 32 anagogical passage the second reading uses stands inside Bellarmine's own Psalm 32 section and not, as a naive search suggests, under Psalm 118, so nothing here is misattributed. This is the class of defect the leaf has already fixed at advisory: HOM-001 stands against the homily's References for naming Migne without saying that a tracked digital transcription, not the printed columns, was read.
findings.required_result: The apparatus or the References say through what the O'Sullivan English was actually read -- for example by adding Bellarmine's web transcription to the 'Reception' paragraph's list of deliveries, or by giving the References entry the stable locator the source binding already holds -- so that no reader takes a reading of the 1866 printing to have been performed when it was not.

summary: Reviewed the expansive study at src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/main.tex (all nine section components, format.tex and the shared preamble), verifying the packet's seal first: all nineteen sealed files hash as REVIEW_INPUTS states. Rebuilt the PDF independently from those bytes (38 physical pages, within 20-50; about 18,900 words). The three readings are distinguishable and internally coherent, each anchored differently (the Gospel's first half and the Epistle's appeal; the Gospel's second half with Eph 4:5-6 and the Gradual's versicle; the Introit, Offertory, Alleluia and Communion), each carries all ten appointed elements, each develops substantive contributions from far more than two checked witnesses, each addresses its strongest difficulty in a named subsection, and each closes with four senses in which the literal and anagogical do real work distinct from the moral. Evidence checked against tracked payloads rather than against the leaf's own records: Gregory Hom. in Ev. XXXVIII.10 (lection heading Matth. XXII, 1-13; 'sicut in duobus lignis', 'non enim jubetur quisque quantum diligat, sed ex quanto', the twice-dyed scarlet of Exod 26:1, the commandment cited from Mark 12:30) verbatim; Augustine on Pss 32, 101 and 109 verbatim at the cited enarratio, sermo and paragraph, including the Gradual lemma 'Dominus Deus eorum ... quem elegit Dominus' and the Alleluia lemma 'perveniat' that the study says the Missal follows against the Clementine; Jerome In Danielem at 9:2, 9:5, 9:7-8, 9:17, 9:20-21 and the seventy weeks, eight quotations verbatim at their stated verses; Aquinas Super Ephesios c. 4 ('conjunctio animorum', the three reasons for one baptism, 'misericorditer expectari') and Super Philippenses on 4:6 ('cum fiducia impetrandi, et hoc ex Dei misericordia', citing Dan 9:18 in the Vulgate's words) in the tracked Dessain 1857 OCR; Bellarmine on Pss 32, 75, 101 and 118 in the tracked O'Sullivan text, ten quotations verbatim and the Ps 32 anagogical passage confirmed inside Bellarmine's own Psalm 32 section; Schuster on this Sunday verbatim (the Good Friday Lateran-to-Sessorian procession, 'whether by coincidence or design', the Alleluia preceding almost all solemn prayers, the Offertory as Rome under the Lombards, offered as his own suggestion); Wilson's Gregorian Supplement sect. XXXVI on printed p. 175, which carries all three orations and whose footnote 'dominum deum O' is exactly the manuscript variant the study reports, with the Postcommunion at printed pp. 32 and 47 and 'sempiterna' at p. 47 as stated; Cassiodorus on Ps 101 and Rupert PL 170 XII.17 verbatim. Cross-references to the Missal all hold against tracked calendar data: the Mass of St John of God (8 March) does read Mt 22:34-46 and its Collect does end 'ut igne caritatis tuae vitia nostra curentur, et remedia nobis aeterna proveniant'; the Jane Frances postcommunion 'facias terrena despicere, et te solum Deum pura mente sectari' stands in the tracked Missal text; the Pauline course and the Matthew pericopes at the Sixteenth, Eighteenth, Nineteenth, Twentieth, Twenty-first and Twenty-second Sundays are correct in every particular, including Luke 14:1-11 on the Sixteenth, which is what the claim about the Gospel's move eight days earlier rests on; 20 September 2026 and the Eustace commemoration are right. The printed Latin of all ten elements matches propers/verified.md exactly, and the English routes (Douay-Rheims at canonical verses, Cummiskey 1861 for the orations, neither an approved liturgical translation) are identified accurately. The chronology appendix prints only generated \chronodate/\chronologyannotation cells, inventories each of the seven appointed Scriptures once in canonical then verse order, preserves the corpus's disputed and research-pending states, and is the fuller reviewed home of the concise companion's page 2. No structural wrapper, no padding, no gallery or proposal appendix, no global four-senses table. Source roles are kept honest throughout: Gregory is said to expound the parable and cite Mark, Irenaeus to use the verse and not expound the psalm, Cassiodorus's Daniel link is marked as his own, and Rupert and Durandus are confined to the chants they share because their office had Luke 14. Limits of this review: Theodoret, Hilary, Irenaeus, Basil, Chrysostom's English, Cassiodorus on Pss 32, 75 and 118, the Gelasian at Wilson pp. 231-232, Guerangerand Durandus have no tracked payload covering the cited loci here, so those attributions were checked for internal coherence and disclosed delivery but not collated at source; the Migne PG and CSEL readings and the CMAA page images were likewise not re-read. The two findings below are advisory and gate nothing. No blocking defect remains.
